newsitem.title: UK: Stg Eurobonds line up as UK election dust settles.
newsitem.headline: Stg Eurobonds line up as UK election dust settles.

text.p: Sterling Eurobond supply picked up on Friday with the end of the pre-election waiting period and issuance is seen stepping up next week with a number of deals in the wings, syndicate officials said.
The Labour party came to power in a landslide election victory which toppled the Conservative party after 18 years of rule.
"Now that the unknown element and uncertainty is out of the market there are sterling deals in the pipeline and business will pick up," a syndicate manager said.

"The tone is better than it has been for some time. A Labour government might create the perception of moving closer to Europe which could attract people to have a punt in the sterling market," he added.
Bradford and Bingley Building Society were first off the block on Friday to launch a 100 million stg 10-year bond via HSBC.
The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp came later with a 250 million stg three-year bond via Yamaichi. Other U.S. agencies were also eyeing the stg sector, some with a global bond in mind, dealers said.
German banks are also said to be looking for opportunities in the sterling sector.
British cables and cables systems manufacturer BICC Plc is mooted to be eyeing 10-year sterling. HSBC and SBC Warburg were tipped as joint lead managers for the transaction.
Castle Transmission Services is expected to launch the first sterling-denominated junk bond -- a 100 million stg bond via CSFB and JP Morgan with roadshows next week.
There is also speculation of a bond for Sutton Bridge Power which is owned by Enron Corp.
The British utility sector could also turn to the Eurobond market later this year if the Labour Party levies a larger-than-expected windfall tax.

Labour has also pledged to continue public/private partnerships through the Private Finance Initiative (PFI), started up by the Conservative government to fund public infrastructure projects with private funds.
Deals in the pipeline include a two billion stg sell-off of the student loan portfolio and the sale of Department of Social Security office properties.

Issuance volumes of sterling Eurobonds surged in the first quarter of 1997, with European retail investors attracted by the yield pick-up over other European currencies and the strength of the currency.
More than $26 billion equivalent of new bonds were launched, compared with $14 billion in the first quarter of 1996, Capital DATA Bondware figures showed.
Meanwhile sterling Eurobond traders were unruffled by Labour's victory on Friday with spreads moving little during the day.
